Since $x>2,$ we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}x & >2 \\ -x & <-2 \\ 1-x & <-1.\end{aligned}
$$

This means that $1-x$ is negative for all the values of $x$ that we are considering $(x>2).$ So, we can multiply both sides by $1-x,$ provided that we flip the sign of the inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3x+2}{1-x} & >4 \\ (1-x)\cdot \frac{3x+2}{1-x} & <(1-x)\cdot 4 \\ 3x+2 & <4-4x \\ 7x & <2 \\ x & <\frac{2}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

However, there are no numbers that satisfy both $x>2$ and $x<\frac{2}{7}.$ So, the inequality has no solution.
